claim.pdf_says: Page 155 opens with its own paragraph "Format 3 (reference-modification):" and the next paragraph is "identifier-1  reference-modifier-1". On page 154 the Format 2 body is the paragraph "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1" and nothing follows it on that page.
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 6678: "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):" — the Format 3 label is welded onto the end of the Format 2 body line, before the anchor; the page-155 slice then begins directly with "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1".
claim.why_it_matters: 8.4.3.1.2 is a run of label/body pairs (Format 1 … Format 11). With the label absorbed into the previous body, Format 2's body reads "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):" and Format 3 appears to have no label at all, so any reader or extractor pairing format labels with their general-format bodies mis-attributes both formats.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides, and every quoted string checks out verbatim. PDF, rendered at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v155/spec_p155.png, printed folio 125): the first body line on the page is the standalone paragraph "Format 3 (reference-modification):", and the paragraph beneath it is "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1". The page then continues with Format 4 … Format 11, each as a standalone label paragraph followed by a blank line and its own body paragraph. PDF page 154 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v155b/spec_p154.png, printed folio 124): the page ends with "Format 2 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts):" then the body paragraph "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1"; nothing follows it but the "124 (c)ISO/IEC 2023" footer. So the Format 3 label genuinely belongs to page 155, not 154. Markdown: line 6676 is "Format 2 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts):", 6677 blank, and line 6678 is the single merged paragraph "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):". Line 6680 is . The sliced page-155.md begins its body at line 6 with "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1" and contains no Format 3 label. Adversarial checks, all of which fail to excuse the defect: - Not missing text: the label string is present in the file. But the finding is misplacement plus paragraph-merge, not deletion, and "misplaced-content" is the correct kind. - Not mere page-break furniture. If the label had merely landed on the wrong side of the anchor as its own paragraph, that would be benign attribution noise. It did not: it is joined to the preceding body with a single space, inside one markdown paragraph, so the paragraph boundary between two distinct normative elements is destroyed. - Not house convention. The document contains 162 lines that begin with a standalone "Format N (" label; every other Format label in 8.4.3.1.2 (Formats 1, 2, 4-11) is its own paragraph with blank lines on both sides. Filtering the 83 mid-line "Format N (" hits down to non-prose lines leaves exactly three, and the other two are the identical defect (line 25254, ACCEPT Format 2 body with "Format 3 (screen):" welded on, immediately before ; line 30846, "SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8 Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):" immediately before ). All three sit directly in front of a page anchor, which identifies a systematic page-boundary transcription defect rather than an intentional style. - Meaning does change. A general format is normative syntax. As transcribed, Format 2's general format reads as "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):", i.e. the syntax specification appears to contain the words of the next format's caption; and Format 3's general format "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1" appears under the "## Page 155" heading as an orphan with no caption identifying it as reference-modification. Only cosmetic difference not part of the finding: the PDF prints two spaces in "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1" where the markdown has one.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described; one addition. At specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 6678 the Format 3 caption "Format 3 (reference-modification):" is merged into Format 2's general-format body paragraph ("qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1") and sits before the anchor, whereas the PDF prints it as the first standalone paragraph of page 155 (folio 125), above "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1"; page 154 (folio 124) ends after "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1". Fix: split line 6678 into "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1", a blank line, the page-155 anchor/heading block, then "Format 3 (reference-modification):", a blank line, "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1". This is one instance of a repeating page-boundary merge, so the fix must sweep the siblings: line 25254 (ACCEPT Format 2 body with "Format 3 (screen):" welded on, before ) and line 30846 ("SET { identifier-7 } ... TO identifier-8 Format 10 (data-pointer-arithmetic):", before ).
